macro.regime: Hawkish Warsh debut jolts gold/silver/crypto; broad equities and credit shrug it off -- a rates-driven correction, not a risk-off event
macro.narrative: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote Friday ("In Our Time") delivered the hawkish surprise markets had been bracing for: he said inflation is "still too high" and the Fed has "more work to do," explicitly declined to offer forward guidance, and floated cutting FOMC meetings from 8 to 6 a year -- pushing September hike odds from ~36% to ~57-58% (CME-tracked) and lifting the 2-year Treasury yield 11.8bp to 4.348% and the dollar (DXY +0.5%). The reaction was sharply asymmetric: gold fell 3.24% (GLD to $408.89) and silver 4.38% (SLV to $60.02), with miners amplifying the move (AG/HL/PAAS -3.7% to -4.9%) after a parabolic ~40% month-to-date GDX run into the event -- while the S&P 500 (-0.25% to 7,711.76), Nasdaq (-0.52%) and VIX (-0.55% to 14.43) barely reacted -- a rates/dollar-driven unwind concentrated in the 'debasement trade,' not a broad risk-off event. Rare earths (MP -4.91%, UUUU -6.80%) and crypto (BTC -3.18% to $77,703) also sold off hard Friday. WEEKEND UPDATE (re-researched 30 Aug): the September-hike debate hardened into a genuine two-sided fight rather than settling -- Goldman's Hatzius framed Warsh as focused on delivering 2% PCE inflation, SocGen's Groen now pencils in three hikes (Sept/Dec/Mar-2027, with the last flagged at-risk), while four former Fed economists writing for Brookings argued a September hike remains unlikely (sub-50%) and Paul Krugman dismissed the speech as conventional with little genuinely new; CME-tracked odds are best read as a real coin-flip into the meeting, not a settled hawkish pivot. Separately, US Treasury escalated its Iran sanctions campaign over the weekend (targeting a UAE bank, Banque Misr, over alleged sanctions-evasion processing) and Iran's IRGC publicly asserted 'decisive control' of the Strait of Hormuz, calling US reopening claims false -- UKMTO still rates threat SEVERE with Gulf shipping traffic reduced; the Iran-Oman temporary corridor deal remains unimplemented. Crypto continued soft into the weekend (Fear&Greed 73->68 by Sat, still Greed but decelerating) without a clearly confirmed new leg down beyond Friday's level -- treat as consolidating near $77-78k rather than extending the rout. Early sell-side commentary calling this a sharp correction within an intact precious-metals bull trend (not a regime change) is now two sessions old but still only moderate-confidence given the hardened rate-path disagreement. MONDAY UPDATE (re-researched 31 Aug, ~07:15 SGT): the Hormuz situation moved from rhetoric to confirmed action -- CENTCOM (on record via spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins) struck two Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island on Sunday 30 Aug after IRGC forces were observed prepping rockets and sea mines for the strait, the first US strike on Iran in over a month; this is independently corroborated by CNN, CNBC, Al Jazeera and others, and Iran's IRGC publicly vowed retaliation. A separate single-sourced report (Fox News, one unnamed US official, not corroborated by CENTCOM/Pentagon/Reuters/AP as of this run) claims Iran already retaliated against US forces in Jordan -- treated here as reported-but-unconfirmed, not fact. Oil extended its Sunday-evening futures-reopen gains into Monday's Asia session (Brent briefly above $90, WTI near $85.4, per Bloomberg/Investing.com), a genuine incremental catalyst on top of the already-priced Sunday reopen (WTI +1.77%, Brent +0.55% per our own feed). No new Fed speak, China rare-earth action, or credit-market data point found since Sunday. Cash equities (US/HK/SG) remain closed pre-open at run time, so there is no confirmed broad-equity reaction yet -- historically this conflict's prior strikes have been absorbed by equities while moving oil, and futures were only modestly softer.
